analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי רִיב introduces a quarrel as the next event in the narrative. The paired phrases בֵּין … וּבֵין identify the two parties, Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to יְהִי, the shortened Qal wayyiqtol form, third person masculine singular. The verb agrees with רִיב, “a quarrel.”

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי רִיב means “a quarrel arose.” The paired phrases בֵּין … וּבֵין identify the two parties to the quarrel, Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders.
analysis.morphology: A singular absolute common noun of either gender, with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of וַיְהִי.

analysis.evidence: After רִיב ‘quarrel’, בֵּין introduces Abram’s herders, and וּבֵין introduces Lot’s herders. The paired prepositions identify the two parties to the quarrel.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם means “those who tend Abram’s livestock.” The parallel phrase רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט identifies Lot’s herdsmen as the other party to the dispute.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine plural construct, used substantivally for those who tend livestock.

analysis.evidence: רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם means “the herders of Abram’s livestock.” The parallel phrase רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט identifies Lot’s herders as the other party to the dispute.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state. The following name אַבְרָם identifies the owner.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: The parallel phrases רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם and רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט identify the herders by whose livestock they tend. אַבְרָם names the owner of the first group’s livestock, just as לוֹט names the owner of the second group’s livestock.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct chain רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham
